minutes.headline: Board approved a bar license transfer and an auto dealer license; license fees left unchanged pending a town manager review.
minutes.summary: The board held two licensing hearings and approved both applications, along with amusement licenses and an architectural district appointment. It reviewed a survey of other towns' license fees and asked the town manager for a recommendation before renewal time. Committee reports covered a MART van route change, the stormwater task force, the finance committee's FY2017 budget review, and the school building committee contingency.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved the transfer of an all-alcoholic on-premise license for J&M's Sports Bar to MJ Inc after a hearing.
The board approved automatic amusement, jukebox, common victualer and weekday entertainment licenses in the same hearing.
The board decided to ask the town manager for a recommendation on license fees, with any change made before renewal, probably with notice in the summer.
The board appointed a member to the Architectural Protection District, with a term to expire June 30, 2018.
After a second hearing, the board approved a class two auto dealer license for KC Sales and Service LLC.

why_it_matters: License fees are a source of town revenue, and a survey of other towns' fees is the basis for a possible change that would reach local license holders at renewal.
Licensed businesses such as bars, restaurants and car dealers would be the ones affected by any fee change, and the board has not yet voted on one.
watch_next: The town manager's recommendation on license fees, which the board asked for ahead of license renewal.
Any notice of a fee change, which the board said would probably go out in the summer.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all five licensing and appointment votes, with only name misspellings from the captions. They differ on the license-fee decision (a town manager recommendation versus a cost analysis) and on the license fee survey figures ($36,000 and $55,000 in ours versus $35,000 and $5,000 in the official minutes). The $3,600 rain barrel grant appears only in ours, and the official minutes have several items we lack, including the FY2017 budget presentation and the attendee list.
